Game overview · snapshot of 30 October 2026

Sarno Legends

A family roguelike deckbuilder. Marc and Yola share one deck and one health bar and fight their way up a hospital overrun by zombies. Marc staggers them, Yola cashes in, and every kill plays a real finisher.

Where it standsAt a glance

One full act, start to finish, is built and live. It runs in a phone or desktop browser. You pick a starting bonus, climb a branching hospital floor of fights, elites, rest rooms, a pharmacy and locked-room events, then beat (or lose to) the Shield Guard. Whatever happens, you bank scrap for new weapons.

The ideaPitch and pillars

It copies Slay the Spire's proven rules and numbers, with a small spin. The mechanics are borrowed; the names, card text and art are all ours.

“I would rather copy something proven that works. And add a slight spin to it.” … “I don't need to do something new no other game does.”MARC, setting the direction
PILLAR 1

Both heroes matter

Every card belongs to Marc (red frame) or Yola (teal frame), and that hero plays its animation. Marc's heavy hits leave a zombie Staggered (takes +50% damage), and many of Yola's cards hit harder against Staggered zombies. Both can deal damage, so no hand is ever useless.

PILLAR 2

The kill is the show

The card that lands the killing blow picks the death animation: a collapse, a headshot drop to the knees, or a blast that throws the zombie back. Killing a Staggered zombie plays a slow-motion execution finisher. It's the payoff, and it never slows a turn down.

PILLAR 3

Every hit point is a choice

Zombies always show their next move and its damage. Nothing is random about damage, healing is scarce, and HP carries from room to room. “Even the easy ones, you can want to conserve HP.”

Same world as Marc's other games

The setting comes from Marc's other two Three.js games: yola-zombie (Yola in the hospital) and Sarno Survive (Marc searching the neighbourhood for Arianna). This game reuses their 3D characters, animation clips, weapons, hospital kit and music. Here, Marc and Yola fight together. Why they're together is Marc's call; all story text is still placeholder.

Start to finishHow a run plays

Title→Armory (equip weapons)→Shift Change bonus→Floor map→ Fights · Elites · Supply Closets · Pharmacy · Locked Rooms · Supply Crate→Shield Guard (boss)→Floor Cleared / Overrun→Scrap → new weapons

The map is generated with Slay the Spire's own rules: 15 rows with branching paths. Row 1 is all fights, row 9 is all treasure, and row 15 is all rest rooms before the boss. There are no elites or rests before row 6, and no two of the same special room in a row. The run saves after every room, and Continue picks it back up.

The coreCombat

The turn (Slay the Spire's)

  • 3 energy and 5 cards each turn; cards cost 0–3.
  • Unplayed cards are discarded; the discard pile reshuffles into the draw pile.
  • Block soaks damage until your next turn.
  • One shared party: 80 HP, 99 supplies to start, and the Nurse's Kit (heal 6 after every fight).

Statuses

  • Staggered: takes +50% damage from attacks.
  • Weakened: deals −25% damage.
  • Strength: + damage per hit. Agility: + block per card.
  • Bleed (from the nail and wire bats): damage over time.

The spin: stagger and cash in

Home Run (2 energy) deals 8 and applies 2 Staggered. Then Clean Shot (1 energy) deals 5, or 10 if Staggered, before the +50% even applies. The intended play pattern is a sentence said out loud: “Home Run him, then I Clean Shot.”

Pacing and feel

After Marc's first play (“The attacks all happen so quick. I think it's ok to give them a moment to show what they are doing”), every attack got a wind-up, a fast strike, a short freeze on impact and a follow-through. Light hits take about 1.15 s, heavy ones 1.55 s, pistol shots 1–1.25 s, and zombie attacks about 1 s. A 1×/1.5×/2× speed setting covers players who want it faster. The next card can be played as soon as a hit lands.

  • Kills: a light hit gives a collapse, a pistol gives a headshot drop to the knees, and a heavy hit or shotgun gives a throw-back. A Staggered kill gives an execution finisher with gore burst.
  • Phone first: landscape layout, drag or tap to play, a one-time coach for new players, 44 px tap targets, notch-safe margins, auto-quality for weak phones, and an "incoming damage" chip by the HP bar that says Lethal when the next hit would end the run.
  • Sound: five of Marc's yola-zombie music tracks, a separate hit sound per weapon, and 166 curated CC0 sound effects. No voices (Marc's call).

Build styles

Marc: Breaker

Stagger everything, then hit hard: Overhead Smash, Ground Pound, Jaw Breaker, Batter Up, Grand Slam.

Stack block and turn it into damage: Tackle, Dig In, Fortify, Barbed Wire, Battering Ram. It now wins as often as the stagger build.

Between runsWeapons: the artifact system

Instead of a pile of permanent upgrades, each run earns scrap, whether you win or lose. Scrap buys weapons in the Armory. Each hero equips one. A weapon swaps a starter card for its own card and adds a passive, so it changes how the deck plays rather than making it stronger. That follows Slay the Spire's rule: unlock variety, never raw power.

Scrap earned: 8 per fight, 20 per elite, 40 for the boss, +15 for clearing the floor. If a change ever weakens a weapon, its scrap is refunded.

The numbersBalance

Balance is measured, not guessed. A headless simulator plays thousands of runs with four bots: random, greedy, sensible and expert. The sensible bot plays carefully, sees intents and drafts synergies. Its results are a ceiling for a new human player, since bots don't misclick or forget statuses.

Reading it: individual fights hit their targets. Whole runs are easier than Slay the Spire's for a perfect player, because its healing (Nurse's Kit plus the rest row) covers normal fights. Infection 0 is deliberately left as the forgiving family level, and the difficulty ladder does the rest.

Each level unlocks by winning the one below. Level 2 adds +20% damage and +10% HP to normal zombies; 3 adds +15% damage and +10% HP to elites; 4 adds +20% damage and +30 HP to the boss; 5 makes the Nurse's Kit heal 4 and rest heal 25%. The greedy bot goes from 81% at level 0 to 22% at level 5. The Daily Run gives the whole family the same hospital for the day, with a score to compare.

The card pass: "every card should have a place"

  • Before: 13 reward cards were never picked by the sensible bot, and 9 more under 11%. After: every common and uncommon gets picked in some runs.
  • Changed with Slay the Spire's numbers: Check the Mag, Double Tap (became a Yola cash-in), Kneecap, Quick Shot, Flare, Deep Breath, Triage (cost 1 → 0) and Light on Feet.
  • New: Tough It Out, Wait for It, Barbed Wire and Battering Ram. Together they made Marc's block build ("Bulwark") a real path: 96.7% at Infection 0 and 48% at Infection 5, level with the stagger build.
  • Weapon tunes: Nail Swing 5 → 6, Sledge 14 → 18.
  • A logic review found and fixed 7 rules bugs. The worst: the Pharmacy reused a random roll, so 21 cards could never be sold.
Still unknown, and why the next step is people: how hard it feels to a real family, whether the shared HP bar reads well, whether kids understand Staggered, and whether a run is the right length. The bots can't answer those.

The making ofHow it was built

Designed in conversation with Marc, then built in about a week (23–30 Oct 2026) by Claude (Anthropic's AI) working in parallel agents against a written build contract. Every step was screenshotted into a flip-book.

Design phase

Started as a Raid / Final Fantasy-style turn-based RPG. Moved to a bigger custom deckbuilder (family card sets, shared deck), then settled on copy Slay the Spire's proven rules + a slight spin. Marc: “I like it now.” Engine: Three.js, like his other two games.

Stage 0: scaffold and assets

Vite + three.js project and an asset pipeline that copies heroes, zombies, weapons, hospital props, sounds and music out of the other game repos (read-only) and compresses the models from 43 MB to 15 MB. A build contract was written covering every card, zombie, relic and number.

Stage 1: nine modules in parallel

Rules engine and content, run layer (map, rewards, shop, events, saves), a check of the Slay the Spire numbers against the wiki, an adversarial bug review, the balance simulator, the 3D stage and director, the room painter and card-art studio, the UI kit with 13 screens, and audio.

Stage 2: one game

Everything wired together, saving after every room, a debug API, and an autoplay bot that plays whole runs in a real browser (5 runs, 4 wins, 0 errors). Deployed to Vercel.

Stage 3: Marc played it

His notes: “Marc needs to actually face the zombies,” “the finishers need more time to slow motion,” “the attacks all happen so quick.” All three were fixed. Art was pre-baked so phones load about 3× faster, and a first-run coach was added.

Stage 4: balance and everything a human didn't need to judge

The card pass, Infection 0–5, Daily Run, run history, collection, the iPhone save-code backup and installable app, the "end turn with energy left?" warning, auto-quality, and distinct zombie looks.

Since (30 Oct)

  • Voice lines tried (Kokoro TTS), then removed at Marc's request.
  • All five yola-zombie music tracks added; per-weapon hit sounds kept; Yola's gun cards sound like her equipped gun.
  • iPhone touch guard: no more accidental zoom or copy/paste menu mid-fight.
  • Card aiming polish: aims as soon as a card leaves the hand, locks on to the nearest zombie, no jump to the centre.

Tech

  • Stack: Vite + three.js, plain ES modules, a DOM/CSS interface over one WebGL canvas, hosted on Vercel and auto-deployed from GitHub.
  • Code: pure rules engine with seeded random streams (any run can be replayed from its seed) → event list → a "director" that paces animations, effects, HUD and sound.
  • Art: 3D GLB characters and clips from Marc's games (Mixamo / Quaternius rigs). Card art is posed from the real animation clips; rooms and icons are pre-baked to WebP.
  • Checks: 175 rules tests, a balance simulator, and a browser playtest bot that fails on any error or softlock.
  • Licences: Kevin Iglesias clips never ship. Tripo t_ clips are held back until their licence is confirmed. Every downloaded asset is recorded.

In Marc's wordsDecisions so far

“I'm ready to begin building the game … a fully playable loop start to finish like act one of slay the spire. Weapon unlocks can be sort of the artifact system.”MARC, START OF THE BUILD
“I think three js is the right engine.. everything from one game will translate and transfer nicely.”MARC, ON THE ENGINE
“I don't want any voices in the game.”MARC, AFTER HEARING THE TEST VOICES
Deck building: keep it the way Slay the Spire has it.MARC, AFTER THE DECK-SYSTEM DISCUSSION (PARAPHRASED)
  • Copy mechanics and numbers, never Slay the Spire's names, text or art.
  • Shared HP and block for the party (separate HP per hero was considered and set aside as less proven).
  • Healing is Yola's starter relic (Nurse's Kit), scarce elsewhere.
  • Music: Marc's own tracks. Tension on the menu and map, a groove in fights, action for elites and the boss, a calm track for rest, shop and victory, and grief for defeat.
  • Marc decides story beats; every name, line and event text is a placeholder until he approves it.

  • Watch for: difficulty feel, attack speed, finisher length, mis-taps, whether "lock on to nearest zombie" ever grabs the wrong one, frame rate (?debug=1), music picks.
  • Known leftovers: real-iPhone notch check; first-load time.
SOON

Polish ideas (no human needed)

  • A glow trail from the played card to its target; damage numbers synced to the impact.
  • Easier-to-read intents (a big-hit warning).
  • Softer transitions between map, fight and rewards.
MARC'S CALLS

Open decisions

  • Story: why Marc and Yola fight together in the hospital; the events' text; floor names.
  • Family: one "call-in" card per run with a painted portrait cut-in (recommended), or a full card set per family member (Marc's bigger idea, parked).
  • Difficulty: keep Infection 0 this forgiving, or make it bite?

Bigger ideas, parked until the core is proven fun

  • More floors (acts): wards, then the basement, each with its own boss: a looter leader, or Adam turning mid-fight (he has both pistol and zombie animations).
  • Chapter-2 characters: looter enemies (pistol, cover = block, reloading gives you a free turn); zombified survivors Bryce, David and Remy; friendly faces running the shop or events.
  • Family: kids "at home" giving a small run buff; call-in cards.
  • More weapons and tiers; Infection 6+ (start hurt, more enemy HP); a draw-on-finisher bonus (to test, not decided).
  • A paper test with index cards and dice, one evening with Yola and a kid, to check that the shared HP and the stagger/cash-in loop read well.
Guard rails for new ideas (from the design doc): test every idea against the three pillars (both heroes matter, the kill is the show, every HP is a choice). Prefer copying a proven mechanic over inventing one. Don't compete on card count (25 first, 60–80 eventually) or piles of systems. Prefer buffs over nerfs, and leave a few broken combos in on purpose.

Plain-text summary
SARNO LEGENDS — snapshot 2026-10-30 (main @ 7bc7cbe)
Play: https://sarno-legends.vercel.app   Build flip-book: /build-log/   Repo: github.com/Marcsarno/Sarno-Legends

WHAT IT IS
Family roguelike deckbuilder in Three.js (browser, phone landscape first). Copies Slay the Spire's rules and numbers
with a slight spin; names, text and art are original. Marc and Yola (Marc Sarno's family, same story world as his games
yola-zombie and Sarno Survive) share ONE deck and ONE 80-HP bar and fight zombies floor by floor up a hospital.

THE SPIN
1. Two heroes, one deck, one HP bar: each card is Marc's (red) or Yola's (teal) and that hero animates it.
2. Marc staggers (Vulnerable, +50% damage), Yola cashes in (bonus damage vs Staggered). Soft split: both deal damage.
3. The kill is the show: the killing card picks the death animation; a Staggered kill plays a slow-mo finisher.
4. Yola's healing is the starter relic (Nurse's Kit: heal 6 after each fight).
5. Meta = weapons bought with scrap (earned win or lose): 9 weapons, each swaps a starter card + adds a passive.

BUILT (act 1 complete)
Title, Armory, Shift Change (run-start bonus), StS-rule map (15 rows), fights, elites, Supply Closet (rest/upgrade),
Pharmacy (shop/removal), 10 locked-room events, supply crates, boss (Shield Guard, 240 HP), victory/defeat, scrap.
Content: 56 reward cards + 11-card starter + 7 weapon cards; 11 zombie types; 17 encounters;
23 relics; 10 medicines; Infection 0-5 (Ascension); Daily Run; run history; collection; saves + save code.
Presentation: painted (oil-filtered) 3D rooms, animated 3D characters, card art posed from real clips, per-weapon hit
sounds, Marc's 5 music tracks, NO voices (Marc's call). 175 tests, bot playtests, balance simulator.

BALANCE (sensible bot, Infection 0): win 99%; HP lost normal 5.2% / elite 22% / boss 44.5% (targets 5-15 / 20-30 / 30-45).
Infection 0-5 win rates: 99/98/98/89/73/60%. Every reward card gets picked; Bulwark (block) build ~ stagger build.

TIMELINE: designed with Marc; built 23-30 Oct 2026 by Claude in stages (scaffold → 9 parallel modules → integration →
Marc's feel notes → balance/polish). Latest: iPhone touch guard, forgiving card aiming.

OPEN / THINKING
Next: family human testing on phones. Marc's calls: story (why they're together), event text, family call-in cards
(1 per run recommended vs full sets per person), difficulty of the family level. Parked: more floors + bosses (looter
leader, Adam turning), chapter-2 looters & zombified survivors (Bryce, David, Remy), more weapons, Infection 6+.
Guard rails: test ideas against the 3 pillars (both heroes matter / the kill is the show / every HP is a choice);
copy proven mechanics; don't compete on card count or system count.
